We recommend the [Google R Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/Rguide.html),
which in turn mostly follows the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/) [@wickham2023tidyverse].
The following principles apply to all R code:

- **Follow tidyverse conventions**: This style is built on the tidyverse style guide,
  which provides comprehensive guidance on naming,
  syntax,
  pipes,
  functions,
  and more
- **Naming**: Use `snake_case` for functions and variables;
  acronyms may be uppercase (e.g., `prep_IDs_data`)
- **Write tidy code**: Keep code clean, readable, and well-organized
- **Decide style here, not by imitation**: Style decisions are made explicitly in this guide
  (or in [psw](https://morrison-lab.github.io/psw/), for writing),
  and code does not copy the style of the code around it.
  When this guide does not say how to write something,
  raise the question as an issue on the psc repository
  instead of copying a neighbouring file
- **Avoid redundant logical comparisons**: Use logical variables directly in conditional statements (e.g., `if (x)` instead of `if (x == TRUE)` or `if (x == 1)`)

{{< include /chapters/coding-style/_pipes.qmd >}}

Many of these rules can be enforced automatically with a `.lintr.R` configuration file;
see the UCD-SERG lab manual's [example](https://github.com/UCD-SERG/lab-manual/blob/main/.lintr.R).
See @sec-style-auto-style for details on automated style checking.
